cards.text: Proverbs opens as the proverbs of Solomon, son of David, king of Israel (Prov 1:1). Here a father talks straight to his son. "My son, do not forget my teaching," he says, and let your heart keep my commandments.

cards.question: The father says his commandments will add something to his son's life if he keeps them. What do they add?

cards.text: Then he names two things his son should never let leave him: loving devotion and faithfulness. Bind them around your neck, he says. Wear them like I wear this apron, friend. I don't take it OFF.

cards.question: Besides binding loving devotion and faithfulness around his neck, where does the father tell his son to write them?

answers.text: On the tablet of his heart
On the doorposts of his house
On a scroll in the temple

cards.question: True or false: The father says holding on to loving devotion and faithfulness brings favor with God but not with people.

cards.text: Now the line folks hang on their walls in fancy fonts: "Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and lean not on your own understanding". Friend, my own understanding once told me the edge of the counter had PLENTY of room, and I hit that kitchen floor like a dropped timer.

cards.question: Instead of leaning on his own understanding, what does the father tell his son to do in all his ways?

answers.text: Ask the elders at the gate

cards.question: If the son acknowledges the LORD in all his ways, the LORD will make his paths ___.

cards.text: Next he says don't be wise in your own eyes. I was wise in my own eyes once, friend, and stamped FORTY cookies with my mustache still hanging in the way. Forty cookies. Forty mustaches.

cards.question: Instead of being wise in his own eyes, what two things does the father tell his son to do?

answers.text: Fear the LORD and turn from evil

cards.question: True or false: The father says fearing the LORD and turning away from evil will bring healing to his son's body.

cards.text: Then he goes there. Money. Honor the LORD with your wealth, he says, and with the firstfruits of all your crops.

cards.question: When the son honors the LORD with his wealth and his firstfruits, what does the father say happens to his barns?

answers.text: They are torn down and rebuilt

cards.text: "My son" again, and here's the part nobody hangs on their wall. Do not reject the discipline of the LORD, the father says, and do not loathe His rebuke.

cards.question: Why does the father tell his son not to reject the LORD's discipline?

answers.text: The LORD disciplines the one He loves
The LORD rewards those who suffer quietly
The LORD's patience will soon run out

cards.question: True or false: The father compares the LORD's discipline to a father disciplining a son he delights in.

cards.text: Now the picture changes: "Blessed is the man who finds wisdom". And from here on, wisdom gets talked about like a person. A she. With a whole RÉSUMÉ coming.

cards.question: The father stacks wisdom up against silver and fine gold and rubies. How does she measure up?

answers.text: She is worth more than all of them
She is worth about the same as them
She is worth less but lasts longer

cards.text: Then he says nothing you desire compares with her. Friend, I'd put a fresh tray of chocolate chip cookies up against ANYTHING, and he's telling me wisdom wins... Okay. Okay. I hear you.
Next, wisdom is pictured holding something in each hand. Riches and honor are in her left.

cards.question: Riches and honor are in wisdom's left hand. What does she hold in her right hand?
The father says all of wisdom's ways are pleasant, and all her paths are ___.

cards.text: Then he calls her "a tree of life to those who embrace her". Those who lay hold of her are blessed.
And then the father zooms WAY out. Past the barns, past the treasure, all the way back to how the LORD made the world.

cards.question: The father says the LORD founded the earth by something. What was it?
True or false: The father says that by the LORD's knowledge the watery depths were sealed shut.

cards.text: The LORD founded the whole earth by wisdom, and that's what this father keeps telling his son to go find. Meanwhile I'm using MY wisdom to remember where I set the timer... and losing.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'Then he names…', 'Bind them around your neck, he says.', 'Wear them like I wear this apron, friend.', 'I don't take it OFF.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new event in the Millers' kitchen: Papa Dorin falling off the counter onto the kitchen floor. The backstory has him catching the cutters at the counter's edge, never falling himself. Jokes may only make up small moments around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank ends the line of 3:6 ('He will make your paths ___'), so the baker has to guess the verse's next word ('straight') rather than reason out its meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'Next he says…', 'I was wise in my own eyes once…', 'Forty cookies.', 'Forty mustaches.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Then he goes there.', 'Money.', 'Honor the LORD with your wealth…'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Multiple choice dominates the stop: 5 of 8 choice cards are multiple choice, against 2 true or false and 1 fill in the blank.

rule.text: No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: 'Now the picture changes…', 'And from here on…', 'A she.', 'With a whole RÉSUMÉ coming.' It also cites only 3:13, but 'from here on, wisdom gets talked about like a person. A she.' uses 3:14-18.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The citation is too narrow. The card describes wisdom being called 'she' from here on, which comes from 3:14-18, but it cites only Proverbs 3:13.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card has five sentences: 'Then he says…', 'Friend, I'd put…', 'Okay.', 'Okay.', 'I hear you.'

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. The right answer 'Long life' is an abstract blessing, like the riches and honor in her left hand. The wrong answers 'A sharp sword' and 'A sealed scroll' are physical objects, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The fill-in-the-blank ends the line of 3:17 ('all her paths are ___'), so the baker has to guess the verse's next word ('peaceful') rather than reason out its meaning.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: 3:20 is only asked as a false statement ('sealed shut'), and no story card tells what the verse actually says: the watery depths were broken open and the clouds dripped with dew. The baker leaves knowing only what didn't happen.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The last card is a recap. It goes back to 3:19 after 3:20 is done and repeats that the LORD founded the earth by wisdom, so it doesn't move the passage forward.

'That's what this father keeps telling his son to go find' stretches the text. The passage says 'Blessed is the man who finds wisdom' (3:13) once. The father never tells his son to go find wisdom, much less repeatedly. The card also cites only 3:19 while drawing on 3:13.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
